hallmark_components: BIS Standard Mark (BIS logo); purity of the article in caratage and fineness; six-digit alphanumeric HUID number
meaning_for_consumer: Confirms third-party assurance that the article's actual gold purity matches what is marked, i.e. 91.6% pure gold
huid_or_identification_info: HUID (Hallmark Unique Identification) is a six-digit alphanumeric number, unique and traceable for each hallmarked item, introduced with effect from 1 July 2021
verification_method: Verify the HUID number using the 'Verify HUID' feature in the official BIS CARE mobile application
consumer_precautions: Each article in a pair, and all detachable parts, must carry hallmarking with different HUIDs; check hallmarking and fineness details on each piece separately
source_page_title: General - Hallmarking FAQs - Bureau of Indian Standards

meaning_for_consumer: Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate content of precious metal in an article, to protect the public against adulteration and obligate manufacturers to maintain legal standards of fineness. Currently, gold and silver are the two precious metals covered under BIS Hallmarking.
source_page_title: Hallmarking overview - Bureau of Indian Standards

meaning_for_consumer: If hallmarked jewellery bought by a consumer is found to be of lower purity than marked, the buyer is entitled to compensation equal to two times the value of the purity shortfall (calculated on the weight of the article), plus reimbursement of testing charges.
verification_method: Get the article re-tested at a BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking Centre
consumer_precautions: Preserve the original hallmarking documentation and purchase invoice
source_page_title: Consumer Protection - Bureau of Indian Standards

hallmark_components: Mandatory marks on hallmarked jewellery (jeweller obligations)
meaning_for_consumer: Under the mandatory hallmarking system, the following marks are compulsory on hallmarked jewellery: (i) BIS Standard Mark/BIS logo, (ii) Purity in carat and fineness, (iii) Six-digit HUID number. The manufacturer or jeweller may additionally put their own mark on the item.
consumer_precautions: Only BIS registered/certified jewellers can approach an Assaying & Hallmarking Centre for hallmarking jewellery on behalf of a customer
source_page_title: Jewellers - Hallmarking FAQs - Bureau of Indian Standards
